name: Question 6
problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=-\frac{1}{2},$ calculate $\text{Var}[\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}X].$ 

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |
worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}X] & ={(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=-\frac{1}{2}.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & =(-2)^{2}\cdot f(-2)+(-1)^{2}\cdot f(-1)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2) \\  & =4(\frac{1}{2})+1(\frac{1}{8})+1(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{13}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{13}{4}-{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{13}{4}-\frac{1}{4} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}X] & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot 3 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall that for any random variable X and constant a, we have

Var[aX]=a2⋅Var[X].

In our case, a=13. Therefore,

Var[13X]=(13)2⋅Var[X]=13⋅Var[X].

We can compute the variance of X using the following formula:

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2

Additionally, we're given that E[X]=−12.

We start by computing E[X2]. Summing up the products of each value of X2 and its associated probability, we get

E[X2]=(−2)2⋅f(−2)+(−1)2⋅f(−1)+12⋅f(1)+22⋅f(2)=4(12)+1(18)+1(18)+4(14)=134.

Therefore,

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2=134−(−12)2=134−14=3.

Finally,

Var[13X]=13⋅Var[X]=13⋅3=1.
